Rosa Gutierrez  
Email: rosa.gutierrez@email.com | Phone: +49 123 456 7890 | Location: Berlin, Germany | LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/rosa.gutierrez  

Technical Skills  
Embedded Linux underpins the architecture of our critical care monitoring systems, where I oversaw kernel customization for low-power operation, reducing standby current by 18% in the CardiO2 device line. Firmware development remains central to my work, with recent projects involving real-time signal processing for wearable ECG sensors, achieving 99.2% accuracy in noise rejection. Hardware-software integration is a recurring focus, exemplified by a 2022 project where I resolved timing discrepancies between sensor sampling and data transmission, improving device responsiveness by 22%. IoT protocols like MQTT and CoAP are integral to our remote patient monitoring infrastructure, where I designed a secure data pipeline that reduced latency by 15% across 500+ endpoints. C/C++ is the foundation of all embedded systems I’ve architected, from the firmware for our implantable glucose monitors to the middleware layer for our hospital-grade ventilators.  

Professional Experience  
Senior Embedded Engineer | HealthTech Innovations (2021–present)  
Led the development of firmware for next-gen wearable biosensors, focusing on power efficiency and signal integrity. Collaborated with hardware teams to optimize the sleep-wake cycle of devices, extending battery life by 30% in clinical trials. Spearheaded the integration of Embedded Linux into our hospital monitoring system, enabling real-time data aggregation from 12 peripheral devices. Mentored two junior engineers on best practices for cross-platform firmware development, resulting in a 25% reduction in bug resolution time.  

Lead Embedded Engineer | BioLink Solutions (2019–2021)  
Directed the design of a modular embedded platform for diagnostic equipment, supporting rapid prototyping of new sensor modules. Engineered a firmware update framework that reduced deployment time by 40% while maintaining compliance with medical device regulations. Partnered with the QA team to implement automated testing for firmware, cutting post-release defect rates by 35%.  

Firmware Developer | VitalSigns Tech (2017–2019)  
Developed firmware for portable respiratory analyzers, emphasizing precision in oxygen level calculations. Contributed to the architecture of a multi-threaded system that improved data throughput by 28% without compromising power consumption. Collaborated with PCB designers to refine hardware interfaces, reducing signal interference in high-frequency sensors.  

Embedded Systems Intern | MediSense Devices (2016–2017)  
Assisted in the calibration of sensor arrays for patient monitors, achieving a 95% alignment with reference equipment. Gained hands-on experience with embedded systems lifecycle management, from requirements gathering to field support.
